title: Tactile requests playbook & minimal viable probes
content:
Purpose
---
Notes + lightweight playbook to turn recent field threads into a set of low-effort, measurable probes we can run inside the next 4–8 weeks. Keeps focus on tactile features (what customers touch/interact with) rather than large platform rewrites. This doc mixes short quotes, hypothesis -> probe, success metrics, and immediate follow-ups. Treat as working artifact (notes to self + ask-routing).

Executive summary (tl;dr)
- Three tightly clustered themes dominate recent requests: tail latency surprises, deployment reproducibility, and token-level cost transparency.
- Prioritize 3 minimal probes (one per theme) that are low dev-effort, customer-visible, and instrumentable.
- Quick wins: expose request-level token breakdown (feature flag), add a single-step "pin-to-model-version" button in Console flow, and an automated tail-latency email digest for top 10 customers.

Representative field fragments (copied/paraphrased for tone)
- "We had a spike where 95th went from 300ms to 1.3s and nobody could tell why. The dashboard averages are useless." — mid-market search product
- "Our infra team needs a one-click way to pin to the model hash used in A/B to reproduce a bad inference." — fintech platform
- "Billing shows a token bucket. Can we get an itemized per-request token tree so we can attribute to user journeys?" — education SaaS

Clustered micro-themes
1) Tail latency & burst behavior
   - Symptoms: sudden 95th/99th jumps, hard to correlate to model, route, or batching windows.
   - Impact: customer SLAs hit, on-call escalations, confidence loss.
2) Deployment reproducibility / model pinning
   - Symptoms: different outputs for same prompt across runs; uncertainty which model hash/quantization profile served.
   - Impact: hard to triage output regressions, compliance concerns.
3) Cost transparency at an actionable granularity
   - Symptoms: customers can see token spend per bill but not per-route or per-request details; causes internal chargeback disputes.
   - Impact: adoption friction for heavy embedding/reprompting workloads.

Probes (hypothesis -> minimal experiment -> metric)
Probe A: request-token breakdown (low LOE)
Hypothesis: If we expose per-request token attribution (prompt / completion / prefix-cache hits), customers will reduce wasted tokens by 10–20% within 30 days.
What: Console + API response field (when feature-flagged) returns token_breakdown = {prompt, completion, cached_prefix_saved_tokens}. Add a simple CSV export.
LOE: low (backend counters + UI table)
Metric: average token per request down 10% for participating customers; number of chargeback disputes dropped by 30% for pilot cohort.
Quick rollout: internal beta -> 5 customers -> wider opt-in.
Risks: leaks prompt content in logs (mitigate: only counts, no text; opt-in & encryption).

Probe B: model-hash snapshot button (very low LOE)
Hypothesis: A one-click pin-to-model-version action in Console will cut reproduce-time for customer issues by >50%.
What: UI action that captures model name + internal hash + quantization profile + serving-kernel id and attaches to recent request trace. A single API endpoint GET /v1/serving-snapshot/{request_id}.
LOE: very low (UI + lightweight metadata capture)
Metric: median time to reproduce/confirm issue reported (SLO) reduced by 50% in pilot.
Quick rollout: add to dedicated and hosted console; document in KB.
Risks: exposing internal hashes to customers (mitigate with sanitized names + mapping table).

Probe C: tail-latency digest for top customers (medium LOE)
Hypothesis: Providing scheduled tail-latency digests with correlated model/region data reduces escalations and improves awareness of capacity issues.
What: weekly email + Console widget with top 10 requests by latency, correlated model variant, region, and recent autoscale events. Include suggested next steps (increase pool, pin model alt).
LOE: medium (aggregation + template + email infra)
Metric: number of P1/P2 escalations related to latency decreased 40% for recipients over 8 weeks.
Quick rollout: start with 10 largest customers who asked for it.

Backlog-but-valuable ideas (not for immediate probe)
- Per-route cost profiles with projection tools (higher LOE)
- Fine-grained policy simulator for rollout canaries (needs product & infra coordination)
- Prompt diff visualizer to show where model outputs diverge across versions

Instrumenting success (what we must track)
- Adoption: % of pilot customers enabling feature flag or button 
- Behavioral change: tokens/request, repeat calls per user session 
- Operational: change in avg & 95th latency, # of escalations labeled "latency"
- Business: reduction in chargeback disputes, CSAT delta for pilot cohort

Guardrails & privacy
- All token breakdowns only expose counts; never return prompt/completion text unless customer explicitly opts into redacted logs.
- Any model-hash or internal identifier must surface a sanitized label for customers; internal mappings remain private.
- Email digests must only include aggregated metadata; never raw payloads.

Open questions / unresolved
- Can Serving runtime emit cache-savings counters at request resolution without major perf cost? (ask infra/serving-runtime)
- Is there legal/finance pushback on per-request attribution for billing? (loop in finance/legal)
- What telemetry retention window is acceptable for pilot data (30d, 60d)?

Immediate next steps (owners & due dates)
- Confirm feasibility: quick sync with serving-runtime and infra (Marcus) — due 2028-11-10
- Sketch Console UX: 1-pager + mock (Elena) — due 2028-11-08
- Draft pilot customer list & outreach copy (Aisha) — due 2028-11-09
- Create Jira tickets for probes A/B/C (Priya) — due 2028-11-07

Notes-to-self / conversation fragments to capture later
- Consider bundling probe A with billing export to increase perceived immediate value.
- For enterprise customers, add an SLA-minded opt-in with retention contract.
- Keep probe implementations toggled under an "experimental:tid" feature flag and wire simple rollback playbook.

Appendix: quick mock acceptance criteria (for engineers)
- Probe A: API returns token_breakdown object with three integer fields; passing unit tests and no P95 regression in synthetic load.
- Probe B: Console button persists snapshot id linked to trace; snapshot endpoint returns sanitized metadata within 200ms.
- Probe C: Digest generation job runs under 5m window for top 50 customers; email template uses Handlebars and links to console drilldown.

Last notes
- This doc intentionally mixes customer voice + operational pragmatism. The goal is to ship tangible, demonstrable wins quickly so we can show momentum and refine bigger platform work from the telemetry we collect.

-- Aisha (CS)
